name: extract_stream
description: Extract one data stream of an NTFS volume by inode address to a file with icat (the Sleuth Kit). The stream is streamed straight to `output` (a path under the run, never under inputs/, never overwriting a file already there), never held in memory and never printed. The answer is what a reader cites: output path, size and sha256, image, offset in sectors, the inode address as asked and parsed (entry, attribute type, attribute id: 168 or 168-128-4 names a stream such as an alternate data stream), icat's exit status and its standard error whole in a file beside the output. A failed or timed-out icat leaves what it wrote as <output>.partial and the answer says status failed (exit 1), never an extraction. The same contract as the base pack's icat_extract, without its image catalogue; read the stream with the tool that fits its type.

image.description: Path to the disk image or volume icat can read (an E01 is read through the Sleuth Kit's libewf where it has it)

inode.description: Inode or inode-attribute address to extract, e.g. 168 or 168-128-4

offset.description: Volume offset in SECTORS (icat -o); 0 for a logical volume with no partition table

output.description: The file to write the stream to, under the run directory; refused if it exists or lies under inputs/

timeout_seconds.description: How long to let icat run (default 280)
